test_title: PYST 01: SSC Stenographer - English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 10 Dec 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To get wind of

options.text: To hear a piece of information that someone was trying to keep secret
To escape so that you don't have to pay

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. To hear a piece of information that someone was trying to keep secret.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To get wind of"** means:

 
 
• To hear a piece of information that someone was trying to keep secret. (खबर लगना)
 
• **Example:** The employees got wind of the company's plan to relocate the office to another city before it was officially announced.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. To hear a piece of information that someone was trying to keep secret.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To recover from something** (किसी चीज़ से उबरना):

 
 
• **Example:** It took him a few weeks to recover from the flu.
 
 
 
• **To get into difficulty** (कठिनाई में पड़ना):
 
 
• **Example:** He got into difficulty while trying to swim across the river.
 
 
 
• **To escape so that you don't have to pay** (भाग जाना ताकि भुगतान न करना पड़े):
 
 
• **Example:** The diner dashed out of the restaurant to escape so that he didn't have to pay the bill.
